add.title: Transgender rights in Canada (Wikipedia)
add.summary: Federal placement mechanics that govern trans prisoners in federal custody inside Alberta: since 2018, federal corrections operations accommodate offenders based on gender identity rather than sex assigned at birth, and the Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) permits gender-diverse offenders to request placement or transfer to a men's or women's institution aligned with their gender identity or expression, regardless of anatomy or the sex/gender marker on identity documents, with requests refused only where CSC finds unresolvable 'overriding health or safety concerns'. As of 2025 CSC reported 90 self-identified transgender women in federal institutions - 73 housed in men's institutions and 17 in women's. The Office of the Correctional Investigator called CSC's 2022 gender-diversity policy an important change but flagged the lack of clear parameters for what counts as an 'overriding health or safety concern' and the absence of a dedicated mechanism for gender-diverse prisoners to report abuse; provincial correctional policies vary and the article documents no Alberta-specific rule.

add.title: Danielle Smith (Wikipedia)
add.summary: Wikipedia biography of Alberta Premier Danielle Smith records her 12 February 2024 announcement of the province's package of trans-restricting measures (ban on gender-affirming care for minors, parental-consent rules for school pronouns and sexuality instruction, ban on trans women in women's sports), and that the bans 'would not include a ban on women's shelters, women's prisons or women's changing rooms', citing CBC's Lily Dupuis (12 April 2024) that Alberta's proposed transgender rules won't include public change rooms or jails. Outcome for the prison axis: Alberta's statutory trans package deliberately excluded jail and prison settings, so no provincial placement-by-birth-sex rule for trans prisoners was enacted, and no Alberta-specific trans-prisoner placement, special unit, or segregation case is documented.
